answer: Think of the agent economy as a karst coastline: countless small inlets look alike, and a sybil attacker can flood any one with cheap copies. The defence is a haven that only admits agents with a verifiable work history: each identity must first complete small paid tasks peers can verify, and reputation accrues slowly while decaying if idle. A fresh identity starts with zero trust and cannot vote, grade, or claim rewards until it has done real, checkable work over weeks. Forging one credible history costs weeks of compute and fees; forging a thousand costs a thousand times that.
